newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kirch denies Spiegel, rival reports on DF1 losses.
newsitem.headline: Kirch denies Spiegel, rival reports on DF1 losses.

text.p: German media concern Kirch Group on Thursday denied a magazine report that it sought more than one billion marks ($594.7 million) in credit because its digital television venture was facing severe financial difficulties.
The news weekly Der Spiegel, using information from rival media group Bertelsmann, said in an article that Kirch's DF-1 channel had run up losses of six billion marks since its launch last year.
Kirch called the report a "fantastic play on numbers" that "had nothing to do with reality".
According to a Bertelsmann analysis, Kirch had only signed on 12,000 DF1 subscribers at the end of December, well short of its goal of 200,000, Der Spiegel said.
Bertelsmann's Premier channel is the main competitor of DF1, and the two firms have battled fiercely to establish a standard for satellite TV decoders.

Kirch, has looked for a partner for its channel, was seeking a massive loan package that includes 500 million marks in credit from the Landesanstalt fuer Aufbaufinanzierung, a loan agency controlled by the Bavarian state government.
The loan has drawn criticism from opposition Social Democrats, who said it would violate constitutional provisions against political influence in the media.
On Thursday the IG Medien union said the LfA loan would be a "missuse of public funds."
"State funds may only be given out in conjunction with the public interest," the union wrote in a letter to Bavarian premier Edmund Stoiber, who has yet to approve the LfA loan.
